samples.text: Until the reference data is corrected at source, the period runs on a manual basis: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. The override replaces the faulty lookup for this month only. It was entered by the platform team and checked against the values the valuation needed, and it is the reason the period could be valued at all. The basis for the override is the confirmed fault: stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Because the fault is in one mapping between legacy and cloud agency codes, and the two code sets are not interchangeable, a manual mapping that bypasses the stale entry is a direct and sound substitute for the period. It does not depend on any guess about other systems, and it changes nothing in the valuation logic itself. For teams deciding whether to wait, the position is provisional but usable. Values produced under the override are fit for the period close and do not need to be held

Confirmed cause: stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. The inventory valuation service resolves every agency code through that mapping before it values a record. One stale entry meant that legacy codes and cloud codes no longer matched for the run, and because the two code sets are both live and not interchangeable, the service stopped rather than guessed. The first working explanation was different. It was initially recorded as overnight ERP outage, which fitted the symptom and the overnight timing. That hypothesis was dropped on evidence: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. With the upstream system cleared, the classification against the product hierarchy sync service became control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer.
